A total of $34, 852$ students study at a certain university. The university conducted a survey among a randomly chosen sample of $1, 200$ students about their preference for morning or evening classes. The results are shown in the table below.

|  | Morning | Evening | No Preference | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Freshmen and Sophomores | $280$ | $190$ | $30$ | $500$ |
| Juniors and Seniors | $210$ | $150$ | $40$ | $400$ |
| Graduates | $120$ | $100$ | $80$ | $300$ |
| Total | $610$ | $440$ | $150$ | $1, 200$ |

Which of the following is closest to the difference between the percentage of undergraduates (freshmen, sophomores, juniors, and seniors combined) who preferred morning classes and the percentage of graduate students who preferred morning classes?

A national exam was taken by $82,500$ candidates. From $1, 050$ graded papers, the distribution of results is shown below.

|  | Pass | Fail | Absent | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Urban Schools | $250$ | $170$ | $30$ | $450$ |
| Rural Schools | $230$ | $170$ | $20$ | $420$ |
| Private Schools | $90$ | $70$ | $20$ | $180$ |
| Total | $570$ | $410$ | $70$ | $1, 050$ |

Which of the following is closest to the difference between the percentage of public schools (urban and rural combined) that passed and the percentage of private schools that passed?
